title: Effect of Pericapsular Nerve Group (PENG) Block on Postoperative Pain After Elective Total Hip Arthroplasty – A Prospective, Randomized, Double-Blind Trial
summary:
Hip osteoarthritis is a common condition in older adults that often causes severe pain and requires total hip replacement surgery. Effective pain control after surgery is crucial for early mobilization and rehabilitation. The Pericapsular Nerve Group (PENG) block is a relatively new regional anesthesia technique that can provide targeted pain relief without significantly affecting muscle strength.
This study investigates whether different PENG block techniques – alone or combined with an additional nerve block – can improve pain control after hip replacement surgery. A total of 168 patients will be randomly assigned to one of four groups, receiving different doses of local anesthetics or placebo. The goal is to determine whether the PENG block can improve postoperative analgesia, reduce opioid use, and minimize side effects.

interventions.name: 10 ml Ropivacaine 0.375% (PENG block) + 5 ml Bupivacaine 0.5% (LFCN block)
20 ml Ropivacaine 0.375% (PENG block) + 5 ml Bupivacaine 0.5% (LFCN block)
20 ml Ropivacaine 0.375% (PENG block) + 5 ml NaCl 0.9% (placebo for LFCN block)
20 ml NaCl 0.9% (placebo for PENG block) + 5 ml NaCl 0.9% (placebo for LFCN block)

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
ASA physical status I–III
Scheduled elective total hip arthroplasty under general anesthesia
Written informed consent to participate
Exclusion criteria:
Known allergy to amide-type local anesthetics
Pregnancy or breastfeeding
Body mass index (BMI) <16 or >40 kg/m²
Dementia, delirium, or other cognitive impairment
Anticoagulation without bridging
Chronic opioid use (>60 mg morphine equivalent daily for ≥6 days)
Systemic infection or local infection at puncture site
Severe hepatic insufficiency or acute renal failure
